fixes.explanation: Nope, no warning sign planted in the rubble here. The LORD says, "I will repair its gaps, restore its ruins, and rebuild it as in the days of old…" (Amos 9:11). The ruins are getting fixed, not put on display.
Not this time, friend. Look at the verbs the LORD picks: "restore," "repair," "rebuild" (Amos 9:11). Not one of them is "demolish." Those are all words for fixing, not for tearing down.

Yes! The LORD says it is "…that they may possess the remnant of Edom and all the nations that bear My name…" (Amos 9:12). Edom's remnant is the part of Edom that is left. Then He adds the nations that bear His name, so the promise reaches past Edom.

Good guesses, but not what the verse says. The LORD says they will possess "…the remnant of Edom and all the nations that bear My name…" (Amos 9:12). Philistia and Moab aren't named in that line. Edom is the name to hold onto.

That's a long trip for what the verse says. The LORD says "…the remnant of Edom and all the nations that bear My name…" (Amos 9:12). Egypt and Cush aren't named in that line. I'd pack a lighter bag, friend, and look to Edom's remnant and the nations that bear His name.

That's it, baker. "…the plowman will overtake the reaper and the treader of grapes, the sower of seed." (Amos 9:13). The plowman is already showing up while the reaper is still out working. The picture is one job running right into the next.

Flip that one over, friend. A plowman overtaking the reaper means plowing is catching up fast, not sitting around (Amos 9:13). Nothing in the verse has a field waiting years for anybody. The verse has the plowman overtaking the reaper.

Good guess if you were picturing a slow harvest, but the verse goes the other way. "…the plowman will overtake the reaper…" (Amos 9:13). The verse says nothing about grain left in the field. What it pictures is the plowman catching up with the reaper.
I get it, selling is what people do with fixed-up places. But that's not in the verse. The LORD says, "they will rebuild and inhabit the ruined cities." (Amos 9:14). Inhabit means they live in them.

It's actually True, friend. The LORD says, "They will plant vineyards and drink their wine; they will make gardens and eat their fruit." (Amos 9:14). Same people planting, same people drinking. Compare that with Amos 5:11, where they plant vineyards but will not drink their wine.
